ores.geology: sedimentary / BIF-derived & supergene; gangue silica, alumina, P
ores.extraction: Carbothermic reduction in blast furnace with coke + limestone to pig iron; or gas/H2 direct reduction (DRI) in a shaft furnace.
ores.notes: High-grade 'red ore' is direct-shipping and can skip magnetic beneficiation, going straight to sinter.

ores.geology: magmatic / skarn / metamorphic BIF; gangue silica, apatite, Ti/V oxides
ores.intermediate: pellets (oxidize exothermically to hematite on firing)
ores.extraction: Pellets reduced in blast furnace (carbothermic) or DRI shaft; strong ferrimagnetism makes concentration cheap.
ores.final_product: pig iron / steel; DRI for EAF
ores.notes: Its magnetism is the whole game: grind fine, pull iron out with magnets for cheap concentration versus hematite.

ores.geology: supergene / lateritic weathering (gossan); gangue clay, silica, high LOI
ores.extraction: Calcine/roast to drive off structural water to a porous oxide, then blast-furnace carbothermic reduction.
ores.notes: Loses ~10-12% mass as bound water on heating (high LOI), so a roast/calcine step is nearly mandatory before smelting.

ores.geology: sedimentary / hydrothermal vein carbonate; gangue calcite, silica, clay
ores.extraction: Calcination (FeCO3 → FeO + CO2) yields porous iron oxide, then blast-furnace carbothermic reduction.
ores.notes: Calcining off CO2 both upgrades the ore (48% to 60%+ Fe) and renders it magnetic for separation — two wins from one roast.

ores.geology: Precambrian banded iron formation (BIF); gangue dominantly chert/quartz
ores.extraction: Fine grind to liberate oxide from chert, wet magnetic separation (+ WHIMS/flotation for hematite), pelletize, then blast furnace or DRI shaft.
ores.final_product: pig iron / steel; DRI-grade pellets for EAF
ores.notes: Below blast-furnace cutoff grade (~25-30% Fe raw) until ground to powder, magnetically separated, and pelletized — backbone of the Mesabi Range.

ores.geology: sedimentary / supergene oxide deposits and nodules; gangue silica, Fe oxides, clay
ores.intermediate: ferromanganese / silicomanganese; or MnSO4 leach liquor
ores.extraction: (a) carbothermic reduction in submerged-arc furnace to FeMn/SiMn; (b) reductive acid leach to MnSO4 then electrowinning to EMM (metal) or EMD (battery MnO2).
ores.final_product: ferromanganese / silicomanganese; electrolytic Mn metal (EMM); electrolytic MnO2 (EMD)
ores.notes: Dual-fate ore: the same MnO2 feeds either the steel-alloy furnace or, via leach + electrowinning, alkaline-battery EMD.

ores.geology: hydrothermal vein / metasedimentary carbonate; gangue calcite, silica, Fe carbonate
ores.extraction: Calcine (MnCO3 → MnO + CO2) then carbothermic reduction in a submerged-arc furnace; or acid leach to MnSO4 then electrowinning.
ores.final_product: ferromanganese / silicomanganese; EMM via leach route
ores.notes: Must be calcined/nodulized to expel CO2 before smelting — Autlán's Molango rotary kiln is the real-world flagship.

ores.geology: supergene weathering-zone hard botryoidal oxide ('black hematite'); gangue silica, Fe/Mn oxides
ores.extraction: Carbothermic reduction in a submerged-arc furnace; bound water and barium report to slag.
ores.notes: Hard and dense (Mohs 5-6), so tough grinding, and its barium content loads the slag chemistry.

ores.geology: magmatic cumulate layers / podiform bodies in mafic-ultramafic intrusions (Bushveld); gangue serpentine, pyroxene, olivine
ores.extraction: Carbothermic reduction of chromite by coke in a submerged-arc furnace (~1700 °C, silica flux); Cr and Fe oxides reduce together, so the product is an Fe-Cr alloy.
ores.final_product: ferrochrome (HC/charge); Cr metal via aluminothermic/electrolytic refining
ores.notes: Chromium's only commercial ore — Fe reduces alongside Cr, so you get ferrochrome unless you add an aluminothermic/electrolytic step for pure Cr.

ores.geology: magmatic sulfide deposits in mafic/ultramafic intrusions (Sudbury, Norilsk); gangue pyrrhotite + silicates
ores.extraction: Roast/partial oxidation + smelt to a furnace matte, convert off Fe/S, then refine by pressure (Sherritt-Gordon) or chloride leach + electrowinning, or Mond carbonyl, to Class 1 metal.
ores.final_product: Class 1 nickel metal; nickel sulfate for batteries
ores.notes: Co and PGMs ride along as high-value byproducts of the Ni refinery — one of the two main primary cobalt sources alongside Cu-Co ores.

ores.geology: supergene weathering profile over ultramafics, upper iron-rich zone; gangue Fe oxyhydroxides, quartz
ores.extraction: HPAL (high-pressure acid leach, H2SO4 autoclave ~245-270 °C) dissolves Ni+Co and reprecipitates Fe as hematite; recover Ni/Co as MHP/MSP, re-leach, solvent-extract, electrowin.
ores.final_product: nickel sulfate / Class 1 nickel; cobalt co-product
ores.notes: Lattice-bound Ni can't be floated; low Ni grade but high Co makes limonite a key laterite source of battery cobalt.

ores.geology: lower silicate-rich saprolite zone of laterite profile over ultramafics; gangue serpentine, Mg silicates, quartz
ores.extraction: Pyrometallurgical RKEF: rotary kiln (drying/calcination + pre-reduction) then electric-furnace smelting with carbothermic reduction to ferronickel; alt Caron process = reduction roast + ammoniacal leach.
ores.notes: High-MgO saprolite is too silica/magnesia-rich for economic acid leaching, so it goes the energy-intensive smelting route — same metal, a different tech tree from limonite by ore depth/chemistry.

ores.geology: high-temperature hydrothermal veins / contact-metamorphic sulfide deposits; gangue sulfides, arsenides, carbonates
ores.extraction: Roast to drive off arsenic (As2O3) and sulfur, then leach, remove As/Fe by precipitation, solvent-extract, and electrowin to metal.
ores.notes: A minor, historically important ore — its arsenic (naming it from Kobold, 'goblin') is both a smelting hazard and a flavorful gameplay penalty.

ores.geology: secondary supergene oxidation crust on Co-As primary ores (cobaltite, skutterudite); gangue gossan/oxidized vein material
ores.extraction: Acid leach the arsenate, remove As by precipitation, then solvent extraction + electrowinning.
ores.notes: Not an economic ore itself — its vivid pink 'cobalt bloom' is a prospector's indicator pointing to richer Co-As ore below.

ores.geology: sediment-hosted stratiform Cu-Co deposits (Central African Copperbelt); gangue dolomite, silicates
ores.intermediate: Co-loaded raffinate / cobalt hydroxide precipitate downstream of the Cu SX-EW circuit
ores.extraction: Sulfuric-acid leach (± reductant for oxide heterogenite); Cu recovered by SX + electrowinning; Co recovered from raffinate by further SX + precipitation as Co(OH)2 and/or electrowinning.
ores.final_product: cobalt metal / cobalt hydroxide; copper cathode (main product)
ores.notes: The DRC Copperbelt supplies most world cobalt purely as a copper byproduct — in a tech tree, gate Co behind Cu (or Ni) rather than mining it standalone.

ores.geology: porphyry copper/molybdenum deposits; quartz-sericite/potassic alteration gangue
ores.extraction: Oxidative roast of MoS2 (→ MoO3 + SO2) with Re recovered from flue gas; MoO3 either H2-reduced to Mo metal powder or silico/aluminothermically reduced to ferromolybdenum.
ores.notes: Chiefly a byproduct of porphyry copper flotation, tying Mo to the Cu circuit, and the roaster is the only economic rhenium source.

ores.geology: hydrothermal quartz veins / greisen associated with granites; cassiterite-quartz gangue
ores.extraction: Alkaline (NaOH/soda) digestion or salt roast to sodium tungstate; purify by ion exchange / solvent extraction; crystallize APT; calcine to WO3; H2-reduce to W powder, or EAF-smelt to ferrotungsten.
ores.notes: Dense and weakly paramagnetic, so gravity + magnetic separation cleanly splits it from associated cassiterite (tin).

ores.geology: contact-metamorphic skarn deposits; calc-silicate (garnet-pyroxene) gangue
ores.extraction: Acid (HCl) or alkaline (soda autoclave) decomposition to tungstic acid / sodium tungstate; purify by IX / SX; crystallize APT; calcine to WO3; H2-reduce to W powder or EAF-smelt to ferrotungsten.
ores.notes: Non-magnetic Ca-tungstate so it routes through flotation rather than magnetic separation — both W ores converge on the same APT → WO3 intermediate.

ores.formula: Fe3O4 (V substituting in lattice; Ti as ilmenite exsolution)
ores.geology: layered mafic/ultramafic intrusions (magmatic); silicate (plagioclase-pyroxene) gangue
ores.extraction: Smelt to V-bearing pig iron; oxygen-blow the hot metal to concentrate V into a vanadium slag; salt-roast + water-leach the slag to sodium metavanadate, precipitate ammonium metavanadate, calcine to V2O5, then aluminothermically reduce (Al + Fe + lime) to ferrovanadium.
ores.notes: Cross-links three commodities — iron is the main product, vanadium rides in the steelmaking slag, titanium reports to the smelting slag; the dominant primary V source globally.

ores.geology: secondary oxidation zone of lead deposits (arid regions); limonite/clay gossan gangue
ores.extraction: Decompose/smelt or leach to separate Pb from V; the vanadium solution is salt-roast/leached, precipitated as ammonium metavanadate, calcined to V2O5, then aluminothermically reduced to ferrovanadium.
ores.notes: A lead vanadate from oxidized Pb orebodies — vanadium and lead are inseparable here, making it a dual-metal node; minor/historic ore today.

ores.geology: sandstone-hosted (roll-front) sedimentary U-V deposits; sandstone/clay gangue
ores.extraction: Acid (H2SO4) or alkaline (carbonate) leach dissolves both U and V; separate by solvent extraction / ion exchange; precipitate and calcine V to V2O5 (then aluminothermic FeV), precipitate U as yellowcake (U3O8).
ores.notes: The classic U-V coupling (Colorado Plateau) links the vanadium chain directly to the uranium/nuclear chain, each historically the other's byproduct.

ores.geology: heavy-mineral beach/dune sands (placer) and magmatic hard-rock; quartz/silicate sand gangue
ores.extraction: Electric-furnace smelt with carbon to high-TiO2 slag (+ pig iron), or remove Fe to synthetic rutile; then chloride route (carbochlorination to TiCl4, Kroll Mg reduction to sponge) or sulfate route (H2SO4 digest, hydrolysis, calcine to pigment).
ores.notes: ~90% of titanium ends as TiO2 pigment, not metal; ilmenite is the dominant feedstock and the smelter co-produces iron.

ores.geology: heavy-mineral beach/placer sands and metamorphic hard-rock; quartz sand gangue
ores.extraction: Carbochlorination (TiO2 + C + Cl2 → TiCl4 + CO/CO2); distill TiCl4; Kroll magnesium reduction to titanium sponge (MgCl2 byproduct electrolyzed back to Mg + Cl2).
ores.final_product: titanium sponge / high-grade TiO2 pigment (chloride process)
ores.notes: Highest-grade natural Ti feed (~95% TiO2), so it skips smelting and feeds the clean chloride/Kroll route directly, with an internal Mg/Cl2 recycle via MgCl2 electrolysis.

ores.geology: weathered placer/beach sands (alteration product of ilmenite); quartz sand gangue
ores.extraction: Carbochlorination to TiCl4 then Kroll reduction to sponge, or blended into slag/synthetic-rutile and pigment feed; grade sits between ilmenite and rutile.
ores.notes: Nature's own 'pre-beneficiated' ilmenite — weathering already stripped much of the iron, giving a free TiO2 upgrade between ilmenite and rutile grades.

ores.geology: Primary hypogene copper-iron sulfide; the most abundant copper ore mineral, found in porphyry and volcanogenic massive sulfide deposits.
ores.extraction: Pyrometallurgical: concentrate smelted to copper matte, converted to blister copper, fire-refined to anode, then electrorefined to cathode. Se/Te/Au/Ag recovered from anode slimes; S captured as sulfuric acid; Mo recovered as molybdenite from flotation.
ores.notes: Dominant global copper source. Cross-links: principal industrial source of Se and Te; significant Au/Ag and Mo byproducts.

ores.geology: Copper-iron sulfide ('peacock ore'); hypogene and supergene enrichment zones of porphyry copper deposits.
ores.extraction: Pyrometallurgical smelting-converting-refining route, as for chalcopyrite.
ores.notes: Higher Cu content than chalcopyrite. Often intergrown with chalcocite in enriched zones.

ores.geology: Secondary copper sulfide formed by supergene enrichment above the water table; high-grade copper mineral.
ores.extraction: Pyrometallurgical (smelt/convert/refine) for concentrate; supergene/secondary ore also amenable to acid heap leach + SX-EW.
ores.notes: High theoretical Cu (~80%). Leaches more readily than chalcopyrite, so often feeds SX-EW.

ores.geology: Secondary copper sulfide of supergene enrichment zones; usually subordinate to chalcocite.
ores.extraction: Pyrometallurgical route; or acid leach + SX-EW for oxidized/secondary ore.
ores.notes: Minor relative to chalcopyrite/chalcocite but a recognized supergene copper mineral.

ores.geology: Green copper carbonate hydroxide; supergene oxidized zone of copper deposits, with azurite, cuprite and native copper.
ores.extraction: Hydrometallurgical: dilute sulfuric acid heap/vat leach to PLS, solvent extraction to upgrade/purify, electrowinning to cathode (SX-EW).
ores.notes: Acid-soluble oxide ore; little to no precious-metal byproduct. ~57% Cu theoretical.

ores.geology: Blue basic copper carbonate; supergene oxidized zone, commonly altering to malachite.
ores.extraction: Hydrometallurgical acid leach to PLS, then SX-EW.
ores.notes: Formula also written 2CuCO3.Cu(OH)2. Acid-soluble oxide ore.

ores.geology: Copper(I) oxide; oxidized zone of copper lodes, associated with native copper, malachite, azurite and iron oxides.
ores.extraction: Hydrometallurgical acid leach to PLS, then SX-EW.
ores.notes: Very high Cu (~88%). Minor but readily leachable oxide ore.

ores.geology: Metallic copper in basalt amygdules and oxidized zones; historically a major source (e.g. Michigan Keweenaw).
ores.extraction: Physical concentration then direct melting and fire/electro refining; no chemical reduction needed.
ores.notes: Already metallic; may carry native silver.

ores.formula: rock: gibbsite Al(OH)3 + boehmite AlO(OH) + diaspore AlO(OH)
ores.geology: Lateritic/karst weathering residue; not a single mineral but a mix of hydrous aluminium oxides with iron oxides, silica and titania.
ores.extraction: Bayer process: hot caustic NaOH digestion (higher T for boehmite/diaspore), clarification (red mud residue), precipitation and calcination to smelter-grade alumina; then Hall-Heroult electrolysis of alumina dissolved in molten cryolite with carbon anodes to primary aluminium.
ores.notes: Bauxite is a ROCK, not a formula. Energy-intensive. Gibbsite digests easiest; diaspore hardest. Red mud is the major residue; Ga recovered from Bayer liquor.

ores.geology: Lead sulfide; the dominant primary lead ore (86.6% Pb), in hydrothermal veins and Pb-Zn-Ag (e.g. SEDEX, MVT) deposits.
ores.extraction: Sinter-roasting oxidizes PbS to PbO sinter (SO2 to acid); sinter reduced with coke in a lead blast furnace (or Imperial Smelting Furnace, co-producing zinc) to lead bullion; refined (Parkes desilvering, etc.).
ores.notes: Silver is the major byproduct and often the economic driver. Cross-links: leading silver source; coupled to zinc via ISP.

ores.geology: Zinc sulfide (ZnS with Fe substitution); the primary zinc ore (~95% of primary zinc), in Pb-Zn-Ag hydrothermal, SEDEX and MVT deposits.
ores.extraction: RLE (dominant, ~85%+): roast concentrate to ZnO calcine (SO2 to sulfuric acid), leach calcine in spent sulfuric electrolyte, purify (cement out Cu/Cd/Co), electrowin zinc onto aluminium cathodes. Minority pyrometallurgical ISP route.
ores.notes: Cross-links: THE dominant source of Cd, In and Ge (tech metals), plus Ga. Pb/Ag report to residues in mixed ores.

ores.geology: Zinc carbonate; secondary mineral in oxidized zones of zinc deposits ('dry bone' / calamine).
ores.extraction: Calcination to ZnO then acid leach, purification and electrowinning (fed into the hydromet circuit); or pyrometallurgical reduction.
ores.notes: Oxidized/secondary zinc ore; historically 'calamine'.

ores.geology: Zinc silicate; oxidized zone of zinc deposits, also called calamine with smithsonite.
ores.extraction: Acid leach, solution purification, then electrowinning.
ores.notes: Silicate oxide ore; requires silica management in the leach circuit.

ores.geology: Tin(IV) oxide; the only significant tin ore (78.8% Sn), in granite-associated hard-rock veins/greisens and alluvial (placer) deposits.
ores.extraction: Gravity concentration exploits high SG (~7); magnetic separation rejects Fe/W minerals. Concentrate reduced by two-stage carbothermic smelting with coal/coke, then thermal/electrolytic refining.
ores.notes: Dense and inert, so gravity-concentrated (placers need little grinding). Hard-rock concentrates may carry Nb/Ta/W byproducts.

ores.geology: Sedimentary (marine) and igneous (e.g. Kola) apatite deposits; phosphorite beds. Carries F in the apatite lattice and trace REE/U.
ores.extraction: Wet process: finely ground rock digested with sulfuric acid; filter off calcium sulfate (phosphogypsum) to leave phosphoric acid. F evolves as SiF4/HF, recovered as H2SiF6; REE recoverable from WPA liquor.
ores.notes: Cross-link hub: sulfuric acid feed ties to ContactProcess; F byproduct (H2SiF6) feeds fluorine chemistry; REE byproduct makes phosphate a secondary rare-earth source. Theoretical F:P2O5 ratio ~0.089.

ores.geology: Bedded marine evaporite deposits (e.g. Saskatchewan, Urals, Zechstein); sylvinite = intergrown sylvite and halite.
ores.intermediate: Amine-float KCl concentrate or pregnant hot brine
ores.extraction: Froth flotation with amine collectors separates KCl from NaCl (~95-96% KCl); OR dissolution-crystallization (hot leach) exploiting steeper KCl temperature-solubility, crystallizing KCl on cooling.
ores.notes: Sylvite = 63% K2O. Flotation tails carry 2.5-3% KCl loss. Alternative beneficiation: heavy-media and electrostatic separation.

ores.geology: Late-stage marine evaporite (most soluble salts); Dead Sea, Qinghai, Zechstein.
ores.extraction: Hot dissolution of crushed carnallite in wash water (~100 C), evaporation, then cooling crystallization (~25 C, vacuum) to drop KCl; MgCl2 stays in mother liquor.
ores.notes: Carnallite = 17% K2O. Energy-intensive dissolution/recrystallization. MgCl2 brine byproduct can feed magnesium chemistry.

ores.geology: Bedded evaporite salt and salt domes; also solution-mined brine and seawater.
ores.intermediate: Purified ~26% NaCl brine (or molten NaCl for metallic Na)
ores.extraction: Chlor-alkali membrane-cell electrolysis of purified brine: Cl2 at anode, NaOH in catholyte, H2 at cathode; cation membrane passes only Na+. Molten-salt Downs cell yields metallic Na + Cl2.
ores.final_product: Chlorine gas + caustic soda (NaOH) + hydrogen; or metallic sodium
ores.notes: TECH-ENABLING. Cl2 feeds PVC/HCl/chlorination (incl. silicon TCS step); NaOH feeds alumina/pulp/soap; HCl loops back. Salt also feeds the Solvay soda-ash process.

ores.geology: Lacustrine evaporite (e.g. Green River WY, Lake Magadi, Beypazari); ~70% Na2CO3 content.
ores.extraction: Calcine crushed trona to decompose sodium sesquicarbonate, driving off CO2 + H2O; dissolve, filter, recrystallize to purified natural soda ash.
ores.notes: Natural route ~30% of world soda ash. Synthetic Solvay route (~70%) uses NaCl + CaCO3 (see soda-ash-synthetic entry).

ores.geology: No ore of its own; feeds are salt brine and limestone.
ores.extraction: Solvay process: brine saturated with ammonia, then CO2 (from limestone calcination) bubbled through to precipitate NaHCO3, which is calcined (~200 C) to Na2CO3; ammonia recovered and recycled.
ores.notes: Dominant (~70%) global route. Cross-links salt (chlor-alkali feedstock) and limestone (CO2 source via calcination).

ores.geology: Evaporite beds; also synthetic phosphogypsum and flue-gas desulfurization (FGD) gypsum.
ores.extraction: Calcination at 150-170 C drives off 1.5 waters: CaSO4·2H2O -> CaSO4·½H2O + 1.5 H2O. Beta form (atmospheric) for board; alpha form (autoclave) for dense high-strength plaster. Harder burn gives anhydrite.
ores.notes: Phosphogypsum from phosphate processing is a synthetic gypsum source; rehydration (setting) reverses the dehydration.

ores.geology: Sedimentary limestone, chalk, marble; near-ubiquitous.
ores.extraction: Calcination ~900 C: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2. Slaking CaO with water -> Ca(OH)2 (exothermic). With clay in rotary kiln, CaO fuses to Portland cement clinker.
ores.final_product: Quicklime -> slaked lime Ca(OH)2; Portland cement clinker
ores.notes: Calcination CO2 is a feed for the Solvay process. Lime is a cross-cutting reagent (pH control, flux, flotation).

ores.geology: Quartzite, vein quartz, high-purity quartz sand; selected for low Fe/Al/B/P.
ores.extraction: (1) Carbothermic reduction: SiO2 + C (coke/coal/charcoal/woodchips) in submerged arc furnace 1500-2000 C -> MG-Si + CO. (2) MG-Si + HCl over Cu catalyst (fluidized bed) -> TCS (SiHCl3), purified by distillation. (3) Siemens process: TCS + H2 CVD onto heated Si seed rods -> ultra-pure polysilicon; HCl recycled.
ores.notes: TECH-ENABLING Si backbone for solar PV and semiconductors. HCl/chlorine step links to the chlor-alkali chain. Highly energy-intensive.

ores.geology: Metamorphic flake graphite in gneiss/marble/schist; amorphous (vein) also exists.
ores.extraction: Froth flotation to concentrate flake; for anodes spheroidize (round flakes), then chemical purification (acid-alkali-acid: H2SO4/H2O2 -> NaOH -> HCl) and/or thermal purification to >99.9% (ideally >99.98%) C.
ores.notes: Purification raises anode specific capacity (~350 vs ~280 mAh/g). Thermal purification (>2500 C) is the high-purity alternative to acid leach.

ores.geology: Weathering/alteration of feldspar and aluminosilicates; primary (residual) and secondary (sedimentary) deposits.
ores.extraction: Wet processing: blunging, hydrocyclone/centrifuge classification, flotation to separate kaolin from feldspar/quartz, acid (bleach) treatment to remove iron staining, dewatering.
ores.notes: ~48% paper, ~52% ceramics/paint/rubber/other. Forms from feldspar weathering (links to feldspar).

ores.geology: Granite, pegmatite, feldspathic sands; most abundant rock-forming mineral group.
ores.extraction: Multi-stage froth flotation (HF or HF-free) to remove mica, iron minerals, then separate feldspar from quartz; magnetic separation for iron.
ores.notes: Acts as a flux (lowers melting point) in ceramics/glass. Can be co-separated with kaolin in fine-particle flotation.

ores.geology: Metamorphic hard-rock garnet and heavy-mineral beach/alluvial sands.
ores.extraction: Crush, size by screening, gravity (spiral/table) and magnetic separation to clean garnet from other heavy minerals; sized into abrasive grades.
ores.notes: Brief abrasive commodity. Hardness ~7-7.5 Mohs; valued over silica sand for low free-silica dust.

ores.geology: Kimberlite/lamproite pipes and alluvial placers.
ores.extraction: Dense-media separation to concentrate, then X-ray luminescence or grease-table sorting; optical/laser sorting for recovery.
ores.notes: Brief abrasive entry. Hardest natural material (10 Mohs); synthetic (HPHT/CVD) diamond dominates abrasive supply.

ores.geology: Lithium-cesium-tantalum (LCT) granitic pegmatites; primary hard-rock Li source (Greenbushes, Pilbara).
ores.extraction: Decrepitation (alpha->beta conversion ~1050 C) then acid roast with concentrated H2SO4 ~250 C to form water-soluble Li2SO4, water leach, remove Mg/Ca/Fe, precipitate Li2CO3 with Na2CO3 (or convert to LiOH).
ores.notes: Formula equivalently LiAlSi2O6. Dominant hard-rock route; beta phase expands ~30% making ore acid-reactive.

ores.geology: Granitic pegmatites; lower Li grade than spodumene, prized for low-iron glass/ceramics.
ores.extraction: Decrepitation then sulfuric acid roast, water leach and precipitation similar to spodumene.
ores.notes: Minor hard-rock Li source.

ores.geology: Li-mica in evolved pegmatites; carries rubidium and cesium credits.
ores.extraction: Sulfate or chloride roast, leach, solvent extraction / ion exchange for Rb/Cs separation, precipitate Li2CO3.
ores.notes: Fluorine content complicates processing; Rb/Cs recovered as byproducts.

ores.geology: Closed-basin salars (Atacama, Hombre Muerto, Uyuni); most abundant Li resource.
ores.extraction: Solar evaporation ponds concentrate brine (>90% water lost), remove Mg/Ca by precipitation, then precipitate battery-grade Li2CO3 with Na2CO3. DLE/ion-exchange sorption is an emerging alternative.
ores.notes: Salar de Atacama supplies >40% of global lithium.

ores.geology: Granitic pegmatites and some metamorphic rocks; ~4-5% Be in industrial beryl.
ores.extraction: Melt and quench (frit) to make ore acid-reactive, grind, react with H2SO4, leach, solvent extraction, precipitate Be(OH)2.
ores.final_product: Be(OH)2 -> Be metal / BeO / Cu-Be alloy
ores.notes: Beryl must be fritted/quenched before acid attack; inert otherwise.

ores.geology: Volcanic tuff deposits (Spor Mountain, Utah); dominant mined Be source despite low grade (<0.5% Be).
ores.extraction: Sulfuric acid leach near boiling, solvent extraction (D2EHPA in kerosene), ammonium carbonate complexation, precipitate Be(OH)2 (SX-carbonate process).
ores.notes: Leached directly without fritting, unlike beryl.

ores.geology: LCT pegmatites and alluvial placers; also recovered from tin slags.
ores.extraction: Digest concentrate in hydrofluoric acid to form soluble heptafluoride complexes, solvent extraction with MIBK separates Ta from Nb, precipitate K2TaF7 / Ta2O5 and Nb2O5, refine to metal.
ores.notes: Columbite is Nb-rich, tantalite Ta-rich; HF + MIBK SX is the standard industrial separation.

ores.geology: Carbonatite complexes (Araxa Brazil, Niobec Canada); dominant Nb source.
ores.extraction: Concentrate reduced aluminothermically or silicothermically with Fe2O3 to ferroniobium for steel; HF route gives purified Nb2O5/Nb metal.
ores.notes: Bulk of world Nb is sold as FeNb for HSLA steel; formula approx (Na,Ca)2Nb2O6(OH,F).

ores.geology: Sedimentary/hydrothermal carbonate deposits; also refractory MgO source.
ores.extraction: Calcine to MgO then silicothermic (Pidgeon) reduction with ferrosilicon under vacuum ~1200 C; Mg vapor condenses as crown metal.
ores.notes: Alternative raw material to dolomite in the Pidgeon process.

ores.geology: Abundant sedimentary carbonate; main Pidgeon-process feedstock.
ores.extraction: Calcine to dolime then silicothermic reduction with ferrosilicon under vacuum (Pidgeon); CaO scavenges silica. Alternatively convert to MgCl2 and electrolyze.
ores.notes: >80% of global primary Mg is Pidgeon silicothermic from dolomite.

ores.geology: Seawater, salt-lake and well brines; effectively inexhaustible Mg source.
ores.extraction: Precipitate Mg(OH)2 with lime/dolime, convert to MgCl2 with HCl, dehydrate, electrolyze molten MgCl2 to Mg metal + Cl2.
ores.notes: Classic electrolytic route (Dow); power-intensive, used where cheap electricity/brine exist.

ores.geology: Rare mineral in zoned LCT pegmatites (Tanco, Manitoba; Bikita, Zimbabwe); primary Cs source.
ores.extraction: Acid digestion (HCl or H2SO4) and leach, remove silica, precipitate/ion-exchange to CsCl or Cs alum; Rb separated by fractional crystallisation or SX.
ores.notes: Hydrated form (Cs,Na)AlSi2O6.H2O; cesium formate drilling fluid is a key product. Rb has no economic primary ore and is recovered here and from lepidolite.

ores.geology: Heavy-mineral-sand placers alongside ilmenite/rutile; the primary Zr source.
ores.extraction: Carbothermic reduction to ZrC/ZrN then chlorination to ZrCl4 (with ~2% HfCl4); solvent extraction (MIBK-thiocyanate or TBP) separates Hf for nuclear-grade Zr; Kroll (Mg) reduction of tetrachloride to sponge, then refine.
ores.final_product: Zr sponge metal; Hf metal; ZrO2
ores.notes: Hf (~2% of Zr) must be removed for reactor-grade Zr due to high neutron cross-section; most zircon used as sand/opacifier/ZrO2 rather than reduced.

ores.geology: No primary ore; recovered from Bayer alumina liquor and zinc processing.
ores.extraction: Recovered by solvent extraction / ion exchange / electrolysis from Bayer liquor or zinc residues.
ores.notes: Cross-link only: model as byproduct of aluminium (bauxite) and zinc chains, not an independent ore.

ores.geology: No primary ore; recovered from sphalerite (ZnS) refining residues and flue dusts (Ge also from coal fly ash).
ores.extraction: Recovered from zinc refining residues by leaching, solvent extraction and precipitation.
ores.notes: Cross-link only: byproduct of the zinc chain.

ores.geology: No primary ore; recovered from copper electrorefining anode slimes.
ores.extraction: Roast/leach copper anode slimes, precipitate and refine Se and Te.
ores.notes: Cross-link only: byproduct of the copper chain.

ores.geology: No primary ore; recovered from MoS2 roaster flue dust, itself a Cu-porphyry byproduct.
ores.extraction: Scrub roaster flue gas, recover perrhenate by ion exchange/solvent extraction, reduce to Re metal.
ores.notes: Cross-link only: byproduct of the molybdenum/copper chain.

ores.geology: Native metal in hydrothermal quartz veins, placers, and disseminated epithermal/orogenic deposits; often alloyed with silver.
ores.extraction: Cyanide leach (CIL/CIP) then carbon adsorption or Merrill-Crowe zinc cementation; smelt to dore; Miller chlorination then Wohlwill electrorefining to fine gold.
ores.notes: Free-milling gold. Carbon adsorption (CIL/CIP) is the default modern recovery; Merrill-Crowe used when silver is high. Dore is impure Au-Ag bullion.

ores.geology: Naturally occurring gold-silver alloy (20-55% Ag) in epithermal vein systems; a primary source of byproduct silver in gold ores.
ores.extraction: Cyanidation; Merrill-Crowe favored due to high silver load; smelt to dore; parting / electrorefining splits Au and Ag.
ores.notes: High silver content overloads carbon-stripping circuits, so Merrill-Crowe zinc cementation is preferred over carbon adsorption. Cross-links gold and silver commodities.

ores.geology: Gold antimonide (pyrite group), ~44.7% Au / 55.3% Sb; forms in post-gold antimony mineralization, e.g. Darasun. Contains no silver.
ores.extraction: Roast to volatilize/oxidize antimony, then cyanidation and carbon adsorption; smelt to dore and refine.
ores.notes: Antimony must be removed (roasting) before cyanidation; antimony reports as a byproduct off-gas/oxide stream.

ores.geology: Submicroscopic/invisible gold finely disseminated and encapsulated within arsenopyrite; direct cyanidation fails without oxidative pretreatment.
ores.extraction: Oxidative pretreatment (pressure oxidation OR bio-oxidation OR roasting) to destroy the sulfide lattice and liberate gold; then cyanidation, CIL/carbon adsorption, dore, refining.
ores.notes: Core refractory-gold gameplay branch. Three competing pretreatments: Roasting (As to As2O3, S to SO2), POX (autoclave 1-3h, up to 99.5% recovery), BioOxidation (bacterial, cheap but slow, ~2% lower recovery). Arsenic is the key hazardous byproduct.

ores.geology: Fine gold encapsulated in pyrite; refractory to direct cyanidation; common in sulfidic orogenic/Carlin-type ores.
ores.extraction: Pressure oxidation / bio-oxidation / roasting to break down pyrite; then cyanidation, CIL/carbon adsorption, dore, refining.
ores.notes: Refractory-gold branch. Same POX/BIOX/Roast fork as arsenopyrite; sulfur reports as SO2 (roasting) or sulfuric acid (POX/BIOX). Alternate pretreatment stages are PressureOxidation or Roasting.

ores.geology: Silver sulfide; argentite is the cubic high-temperature form, acanthite the monoclinic form stable below 177C. Chief primary silver ore mineral, but most silver is byproduct of Pb/Zn/Cu ores.
ores.intermediate: silver concentrate / Pb-Ag-Zn-Cu concentrate; or lead-smelter bullion
ores.extraction: Primary: cyanidation then Merrill-Crowe to dore. Byproduct route: recovered in lead smelting, Parkes desilvering (zinc added, Ag-Zn crust skimmed), cupellation, then Moebius electrorefining.
ores.notes: Silver is overwhelmingly byproduct-driven from Pb/Zn/Cu refining. Parkes process exploits silver's higher solubility in zinc; cupellation oxidizes lead to litharge; Moebius is the silver-nitrate electrorefining analogue of Wohlwill.

ores.geology: Native metal in oxidized zones of hydrothermal deposits; relatively minor compared with byproduct silver from base-metal ores.
ores.extraction: Cyanidation then Merrill-Crowe to dore; cupellation and/or Moebius electrorefining to fine silver.
ores.notes: Like gold, benefits from gravity recovery of coarse metal. Still frequently co-produced with base metals.

ores.geology: Platinum arsenide; principal Pt mineral in Bushveld (Merensky/UG2) and Norilsk/Sudbury Ni-Cu sulfide ores. Associated with base-metal sulfides.
ores.intermediate: Ni-Cu-PGM sulfide flotation concentrate; then PGM matte
ores.extraction: Flotation (xanthate/dithiophosphate, pH 7.5-9) to Ni-Cu-PGM concentrate; smelt to PGM-rich matte; convert and base-metal leach to strip Ni/Cu/Co; pressure-oxidation leach of residue; solvent extraction + ion exchange + selective precipitation to separate the six PGMs; refine.
ores.notes: Deepest refining chain in scope. PGMs are co-products, never recovered alone. Base metals (Ni/Cu/Co) stripped at the matte-leach stage cross-link to the base-metals catalog; arsenic is a sperrylite-specific byproduct.

ores.geology: Platinum sulfide; abundant PGE sulfide in Bushveld Merensky/UG2 reefs alongside braggite and laurite.
ores.intermediate: PGM-bearing sulfide concentrate; then PGM matte
ores.extraction: Flotation with Ni-Cu sulfides; smelt to matte; base-metal removal; PGM refining via dissolution-precipitation, solvent extraction and ion exchange.
ores.notes: Co-produced with all PGMs and base-metal sulfides; shares the Merensky/UG2 flotation-smelt-refine chain with braggite and sperrylite.

ores.geology: Pt-Pd-Ni sulfide; major PGE sulfide of the Bushveld UG2 reef; carries significant palladium.
ores.intermediate: PGM-bearing sulfide concentrate; then PGM matte
ores.extraction: Flotation; smelt to matte; base-metal leach; solvent extraction / ion exchange / precipitation refining chain to separate Pt and Pd.
ores.notes: Ni in the lattice ties it directly to the nickel base-metal circuit; main palladium-bearing primary PGM in UG2.

ores.geology: Mercury(II) sulfide, the near-exclusive mercury ore; forms in low-temperature hydrothermal veins and hot-spring deposits, sometimes with stibnite.
ores.extraction: Roasting/retorting at 500-600C: HgS + O2 yields Hg vapor + SO2; mercury vapor condensed on cooling and collected; distillation for final purity.
ores.notes: Distinctive short chain: oxidative roast/retort volatilizes mercury, which is condensed. Rotary kilns/multiple-hearth furnaces for large tonnage, externally heated retorts for small/fine ore. Emits SO2; can co-occur with antimony (stibnite).

ores.commodity: Mixed light-REE oxides (Ce, La, Nd, Pr)
ores.geology: Fluorocarbonate; main LREE ore. Mountain Pass (California) carbonatite and Bayan Obo (Inner Mongolia, China) where it occurs with iron ore and monazite (bastnäsite:monazite ~9:1 to 1:1). ~65-75% REO.
ores.intermediate: ~60% REO flotation concentrate -> roasted/calcined -> acid or alkaline leach -> mixed RE chloride/nitrate liquor
ores.extraction: Roasting/Calcination to drive off CO2 and oxidize Ce, then Leaching to solution, then multi-stage SolventExtraction cascade to individual REO, then MoltenSaltElectrolysis to metal
ores.final_product: Individual light-REE metals (La, Ce, Pr, Nd); NdPr feed for NdFeB magnets
ores.notes: Flagship LREE ore. Comes out as a MIXED concentrate - element separation happens later in the SX cascade, not in beneficiation. Low Th compared to monazite.

ores.geology: REE phosphate; dense and paramagnetic, concentrates in heavy-mineral sands and carbonatites. LREE-dominant but notable Nd. ~55-60% REO. Carries 5-10%+ ThO2 -> radioactive handling required.
ores.intermediate: RE phosphate cracked by hot NaOH (AlkalineBake, 120-175 C) or H2SO4 (AcidBake, 200-300 C) -> dissolve -> precipitate Th(OH)4 out -> mixed RE liquor
ores.extraction: Cracking(AlkalineBake or AcidBake) to destroy phosphate matrix and liberate Th + REEs, dissolution, selective Th removal, then SolventExtraction cascade to individual REO, then electrolysis / Ca reduction
ores.final_product: Individual light-REE metals; thorium precipitate sequestered/stored
ores.notes: Also a thorium source. Radioactivity/Th handling is mandatory and gameplay-relevant: Th(OH)4 is selectively precipitated (pH control with NaOH/NH4OH) before REEs proceed. Cross-links to the minor/radioactive group (Th).

ores.commodity: Heavy-REE-enriched oxides (Y, Dy, Yb, Er, Gd)
ores.geology: Yttrium phosphate, isostructural with zircon; heavy-REE enriched (Y plus mid/heavy lanthanides substitute for Y). Found in placers and granitic pegmatites. ~54-65% REO.
ores.intermediate: Hot NaOH or H2SO4 bake (more refractory than monazite) -> dissolve -> mixed HRE liquor
ores.extraction: Cracking(AlkalineBake/AcidBake), Leaching, then the hardest SolventExtraction separations (adjacent heavy REEs), then MetallothermicReduction(Ca) or electrolysis
ores.final_product: Y, Dy, Tb, Er, Gd oxides and metals
ores.notes: Primary hard-rock source of heavy REEs. Heavy-REE separations in the SX cascade are the most difficult of all.

ores.formula: REE3+ adsorbed on kaolinite/halloysite/illite (no discrete REE mineral)
ores.commodity: Heavy REEs incl. Dy, Tb, Y (plus some LREE)
ores.geology: Regolith-hosted deposits from weathering of granite, latitudes ~24-26 N in South China. REE3+ ions loosely adsorbed on clay surfaces - NOT a mineral lattice. Accounts for >80% of world medium/heavy REE supply; the dominant Dy/Tb/Y source.
ores.intermediate: In-situ / heap IonExchange leach with (NH4)2SO4 or NaCl displaces REE3+ into solution -> RE sulfate/chloride liquor -> Precipitation (oxalate/carbonate)
ores.extraction: IonExchange leach (no crushing or flotation needed - ions are simply exchanged off the clay), Precipitation, then SolventExtraction cascade to individual heavy REO
ores.final_product: Dy, Tb, Y oxides -> heavy-REE magnet additives and phosphors
ores.notes: The cheap, simple-to-mine but strategically vital heavy-REE source. No frothflotation/grinding - highlights that the separation (SX cascade of Dy/Tb) is the hard part, not extraction from the clay.

ores.geology: Complex perovskite-type oxide; Kola Peninsula (Russia) alkaline massifs. Mined mainly for Ti/Nb/Ta, with REEs as a by-product.
ores.intermediate: Chlorination / acid crack -> separate Ti,Nb,Ta -> RE liquor
ores.extraction: Cracking, Leaching, SolventExtraction for the LREE byproduct stream
ores.notes: Brief coverage - REE is a co-product here. Carries Th (radioactive group).

ores.geology: Brownish-black complex oxide in granitic pegmatites; Nb/Ta-dominant (vs Ti-dominant polycrase). Radioactive (U, Th).
ores.intermediate: Acid or alkaline crack -> RE + Nb/Ta liquor
ores.extraction: Cracking, Leaching, SolventExtraction
ores.notes: Brief coverage. Radioactive U/Th present - links to the minor/radioactive group.

ores.geology: Separated from mixed LREE concentrate (bastnäsite/monazite) by the SX cascade; co-produced with Pr as NdPr.
ores.extraction: From mixed RE liquor: SolventExtraction to isolate Nd, Precipitation (oxalate), Calcination to Nd2O3, then MoltenSaltElectrolysis in a molten NdF3-LiF fluoride bath (~1050 C); iron cathode can yield Nd-Fe alloy directly
ores.notes: The flagship magnet metal. NdFeB = Nd + Pr + Fe + B, with Dy/Tb added for high-temperature coercivity. Main demand driver (EV motors, wind turbines).

ores.geology: Separated from mixed LREE concentrate; usually co-produced with Nd as 'NdPr' / didymium.
ores.extraction: SolventExtraction, Precipitation, Calcination to Pr6O11, MoltenSaltElectrolysis
ores.notes: Magnet metal, typically sold/used together with Nd (NdPr) - the two are hard to fully separate and share end use.

ores.geology: Heavy REE - mainly from ion-adsorption clays and xenotime. One of the HARDEST and most valuable separations.
ores.extraction: Many-stage SolventExtraction (hardest heavy separations), Precipitation, Calcination to Dy2O3, MetallothermicReduction(Ca) of the fluoride
ores.notes: Critical NdFeB additive - keeps magnets coercive at high temperature. Its separation difficulty (adjacent heavy REEs) is the economic crux of the whole chain.

ores.geology: Mid/light-heavy boundary REE, separated from mixed LREE concentrate.
ores.extraction: SolventExtraction, Precipitation, Calcination to Sm2O3, MetallothermicReduction(Ca) (Sm is volatile - reduced with La/Ca, not easily electrowon)
ores.notes: SmCo magnets (Sm + Co) for very high temperature / aerospace & defence applications.

ores.geology: Lightest REE, abundant in bastnäsite/monazite; comes off early in the SX cascade.
ores.extraction: SolventExtraction, Precipitation, Calcination to La2O3, MoltenSaltElectrolysis
ores.notes: FCC petroleum-cracking catalysts and NiMH battery alloys. Cheap, high-volume.

ores.geology: Most abundant REE; easily split off because Ce can be oxidized to Ce(IV) and removed selectively.
ores.extraction: Oxidative separation / SolventExtraction, Precipitation, Calcination to CeO2 (often used as oxide directly)
ores.notes: Glass polishing, auto-exhaust catalysts, UV-absorbing glass. The Ce(IV) oxidation trick makes it the easiest REE to pull out of the mix.

ores.geology: Scarce mid-REE; separable via its reducible Eu(II) state (reduce to Eu2+, precipitate as sulfate).
ores.extraction: SolventExtraction / Eu(II) reduction-precipitation, Calcination to Eu2O3
ores.notes: Red and blue phosphors (displays, fluorescent lighting). High value, low volume.

ores.geology: Grouped with the heavy REEs; dominant element in xenotime and major component of ion-adsorption clays.
ores.extraction: SolventExtraction / IonExchange, Precipitation, Calcination to Y2O3, MetallothermicReduction(Ca)
ores.notes: Phosphor host lattice, YAG, high-temperature ceramics. Behaves as a heavy REE despite low atomic number.

ores.geology: Heavy REE from ion-adsorption clays and xenotime; one of the scarcest and hardest to separate.
ores.extraction: Many-stage SolventExtraction (very hard heavy separation), Precipitation, Calcination to Tb4O7, MetallothermicReduction(Ca)
ores.notes: Magnet additive (like Dy) plus green phosphor. Extremely scarce and expensive - the difficulty of its separation is a core gameplay hook.

ores.geology: Low-temperature hydrothermal veins; principal antimony ore, frequently associated with gold.
ores.intermediate: Sb2O3 (roaster/fumed oxide) or crude antimony oxide
ores.extraction: Rich ore liquated; concentrate given a volatilizing/oxidizing roast to Sb2O3 (volatile ~900-950 C in low-O2 gas; high O2 forms non-volatile SbO2), then carbothermic reduction with soda-ash flux to regulus. Sulfur-fixation roast with ZnO/C avoids SO2.
ores.notes: Often co-recovered with gold. Oxygen control critical to fuming.

ores.geology: Hydrothermal veins with Pb/Cu/Sn/W deposits; bismuth is overwhelmingly a byproduct of those refining streams.
ores.intermediate: Bi2O3 (roaster oxide) or crude bismuth bullion
ores.extraction: Primary sulfide: roast to oxide then coke smelting/carbothermic reduction. Alkaline/molten-salt smelting with Fe2O3 sulfur-fixing agent gives ~96% Bi, co-recovering W/Mo to slag. Mostly recovered as byproduct (debismuthizing of lead, anode slimes).
ores.notes: Supply chain dominated by Pb/Cu/W byproduct recovery rather than primary mining.

ores.geology: Most abundant arsenic ore; high-temperature hydrothermal veins, pegmatites, contact-metamorphic settings. Common impurity in gold/copper ores.
ores.intermediate: As2O3 (white arsenic) condensed from flue gas
ores.extraction: Roast in air to volatilize As2O3, captured in flues/baghouse; metal made by carbothermic reduction of As2O3. Mostly recovered as byproduct from Au/Cu/Pb smelter flue dust.
ores.notes: TOXIC. As2O3 acutely poisonous; off-gas, flue dust, and residue stabilization are key hazards. Largely a byproduct commodity.

ores.geology: Low-temperature hydrothermal and volcanic/hot-spring deposits; arsenic sulfide minerals.
ores.extraction: Roasting in air: 2 As2S3 + 9 O2 -> 2 As2O3 + 6 SO2; As2O3 volatilized and condensed.
ores.notes: TOXIC. Historically used in pigments and traditional medicine; roaster gas handling is hazardous.

ores.geology: Primary uranium oxide (UO2, grading toward U3O8); hydrothermal veins, unconformity and sandstone-hosted deposits. Pitchblende is the massive variety.
ores.intermediate: Uranyl sulfate or uranyl tricarbonate pregnant liquor
ores.extraction: Acid (H2SO4 -> uranyl sulfate) or alkaline (Na2CO3 -> uranyl tricarbonate) leach; purify/concentrate by ion exchange or solvent extraction; precipitate and calcine to yellowcake.
ores.notes: RADIOACTIVE. Radon/radium and tailings are gameplay hazard hooks; yellowcake is a regulated nuclear material.

ores.geology: Uranium silicate; common in reduced sandstone-hosted (roll-front) deposits, often intergrown with uraninite.
ores.extraction: Leach (acid or alkaline), ion exchange / solvent extraction, precipitation, calcination to U3O8.
ores.notes: RADIOACTIVE. Amenable to in-situ recovery (ISR) leaching.

ores.geology: Secondary uranium-vanadium mineral in sandstone-hosted deposits (e.g., Colorado Plateau).
ores.extraction: Salt roast then leach; separate U and V by solvent extraction / ion exchange; precipitate both.
ores.notes: RADIOACTIVE. Dual uranium-vanadium ore.

ores.geology: Thorium oxide in granite pegmatites and metamorphic rocks; very high Th concentration but minor commercial source.
ores.extraction: Acid or alkaline digest/leach; solvent extraction; precipitation; calcination to ThO2.
ores.notes: RADIOACTIVE. Not commercially mined at scale; thorium mainly a monazite byproduct.

ores.geology: RE phosphate in mineral/beach sands; ~3-5% ThO2. Mined primarily for rare earths.
ores.intermediate: Mixed RE/Th sulfate or hydroxide cake
ores.extraction: Acid (conc. H2SO4) or alkaline (NaOH) digest cracks the phosphate; Th separated from REE by selective precipitation / solvent extraction via temperature and acidity control.
ores.notes: RADIOACTIVE. CROSS-LINK: shared feed with the rare-earth catalog; Th is the radioactive co-product of REE recovery.

ores.geology: Continental evaporite deposits near Pliocene lakes and boron-rich brines in arid basins.
ores.extraction: Dissolution, purification, evaporation/recrystallization; acidify with H2SO4 to make boric acid.
ores.notes: Sodium borate purified by dissolution-recrystallization; brine ops use solar evaporation ponds.

ores.geology: Evaporite borate associated with borax beds (e.g., Kramer/Boron, California).
ores.extraction: Dissolution, evaporation and recrystallization to borax/boric acid.
ores.notes: Lower hydration sodium borate; processed similarly to borax.

ores.geology: Calcium borate evaporite (major in Turkey and western USA).
ores.extraction: Acid leach with H2SO4, then precipitation/crystallization of boric acid.
ores.notes: Calcium borate requires acid attack rather than simple recrystallization.

ores.geology: Hydrothermal veins and replacement deposits; gangue often galena/sphalerite/barite.
ores.extraction: React acidspar with concentrated H2SO4 at ~250 C: CaF2 + H2SO4 -> 2 HF + CaSO4; HF purified/scrubbed. Gypsum/anhydrite byproduct.
ores.notes: TOXIC/corrosive intermediate. Acidspar is ~60-65% of global fluorspar output and feeds all fluorochemicals. (Reduction/Refining stages here denote the acid digestion + HF purification; no metallic reduction.)

ores.geology: Caprock of salt domes and volcanic deposits; elemental sulfur.
ores.extraction: Frasch process melts and lifts sulfur with superheated steam and air. Burn S to SO2, then contact process to sulfuric acid.
ores.notes: Frasch dominated supply until ~1970; now largely supplanted by recovered sulfur.

ores.geology: Ubiquitous iron sulfide; hydrothermal, sedimentary, and massive-sulfide deposits.
ores.extraction: Roast: 4 FeS2 + 11 O2 -> 2 Fe2O3 + 8 SO2, leaving iron-oxide cinder; SO2 fed to contact process.
ores.notes: Historic principal sulfur source before Frasch; cinder sometimes used for iron.

ores.geology: Hydrogen sulfide from sour natural gas and refinery streams (not a mineral; gas sweetening feed).
ores.extraction: Claus process: partial oxidation of H2S to SO2, then 2 H2S + SO2 -> 3 S + 2 H2O; tail-gas SO2 can feed contact process.
ores.notes: Dominant modern sulfur source. Included as a feedstock, not a mined mineral.

ores.geology: Hydrothermal veins, bedded sedimentary, and residual deposits; barite group sulfate.
ores.intermediate: BaS (black ash) for chemicals; direct barite for drilling mud
ores.extraction: Most used directly as weighting agent/filler after beneficiation. For chemicals: reduction roast with coke -> BaS (black ash), then leach/precipitate to BaCO3 or BaCl2.
ores.notes: Isostructural with celestine (complete BaSO4-SrSO4 solid solution). Bulk demand is drilling mud, used as-is.

ores.geology: Sedimentary/evaporitic strontium sulfate; barite-group member.
ores.extraction: Black-ash: reduction roast with coke at ~1100-1300 C -> SrS, then carbonation to SrCO3. Or direct conversion: react ground concentrate with Na2CO3 (+ steam) to SrCO3 + Na2SO4.
ores.notes: SrCO3 used in glass, magnets, pyrotechnics. Complete solid solution with barite.
